deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a printed page (p. 382) of the annual report of the Königliche Gesellschaft (Societät) der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen. It evidently comes from the 'Nachrichten von der G. A. Universität und der Königl. Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen' for 1863, in the section on the anniversary meeting. The page was bound or kept within the Riemann bundle 'R.Primzahlen' as Bl. 14v, probably as scrap or wrapper paper. It carries no handwritten annotation by Riemann. The text continues the list of deceased correspondents of the Society begun on p. 381 (Eschricht, Rößler):
(1) Carl Rümker, former director of the Hamburg observatory and navigation school. He died 21 Dec 1862 in Lisbon in his 74th year. He was praised for his observations of the southern sky at Parramatta (1821–1829) and for his catalogue of 12000 fixed stars (1843–1859).
(2) Carl Kreil, director of the Imperial Central Institute for Meteorology and Geomagnetism and professor of physics in Vienna. He died the same day aged 64. From 1831 to 1838 in Milan he was an early member of Gauss's Magnetic Union, and the Vienna Central Institute owes its founding to him.
(3) Peter Andreas Munch, professor of history and national archivist in Christiania. He died 25 May 1863 in Rome in his 52nd year, after more than two years of research in the Vatican archive.
(4) Jacob Geel, librarian at Leiden, a Hellenist and critic. He died 11 Nov 1862.
The page ends with the start of the announcement of newly elected foreign members, which continues on p. 383 (Kopp, von Maurer, and others).
There is no derivation to reconstruct and no problem being served. The page has no connection to prime numbers or to Riemann's mathematical work beyond its physical location in the bundle.
errors: No mathematical content, so no mathematical errors.
Printer's typo in the original: 'unb' for 'und' ('Geschichte unb Reichsarchivar').
The biographical dates agree with standard sources: Rümker 1788–1862, Kreil 1798–1862, Munch 1810–1863, Geel 1789–1862.

results.what: Printed obituary notices of Göttingen Society correspondents (Rümker, Kreil, Munch, Geel) and the start of a list of new foreign members
results.usually_credited_to: Secretary of the Königliche Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen (annual report, Göttinger Nachrichten 1863)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a printed society report with no mathematical content and no annotation by Riemann. Its presence in the bundle is only archival (scrap or wrapper paper).

checkable.asserts: Rümker (born 18 May 1788, died 21 Dec 1862) had completed 74 years, i.e. he was 74 at death. Note: '74. Jahre' strictly means 'in his 74th year'; if read that way the obituary is off by one.
Kreil (born 4 Nov 1798) was 64 years old at death on 21 Dec 1862, as stated.
Munch (born 15 Dec 1810) was 52 at death on 25 May 1863, i.e. in his 53rd year of life. The text says 'im 52. Lebensjahre', which is off by one in the strict reading.
Rümker's stated Parramatta observing span 1821–1829 covers 8 years.

transcription_corrections: The transcription faithfully reproduces the image. 'unb' is a typo in the printed original itself, not an OCR error.
The heading line '— 382 —' and all names (Rümker, Kreil, Munch, Geel, Paramatta, Sidney) match the print.
